newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares seen inching up despite Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares seen inching up despite Deng's death.

text.p: Manila shares are likely to rise on Thursday as the market shifts from second-liners to blue chips and investors would buy despite news of the death of the 93-year old Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, traders said.

"There's likely no effect since the local market has known that while he was living, other people were running the country. It's a remote possibility that if the Hong Kong market reacts we might sympathise ," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.
China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection.

"The news will directly affect the Hong Kong market but whether this will spillover to the Philippines, that remains to be seen. The quicker the situation stabilises, the better it will be for the regional market," said Francisco Trinidad, research head at DBS Securities Philippines Inc.
Traders said the decision of the Court of Appeals on Wednesday lifting the restraining order on the privatisation of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) may perk up the market.
Trinidad said winning bidders for the two MWSS concessions Ayala Corp and Benpres Holdings Corp may be seen as trading buys.

"People who made money in speculatives have started shifting to real stocks yesterday and frustration level of big players who are waiting for the index to drop below 3,300 is increasing, so with or without news they'll likely buy up on blue chips," said Reyes.

Traders said the market on Wednesday saw investor interest returning on some blue chips as the index was lifted by late session buying on Ayala Land, San Miguel Corp and the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co.
